overview: The Council approved a snow removal ordinance and passed a resolution opposing state legislation regarding gig economy worker classification. Members also requested updates on utility construction projects and scheduled a public meeting to address proposed MBTA bus route changes.

items.title: Approval of Records and Committee Reports
items.summary: The Council approved the records of the May 17, 2022 meeting and accepted a report from the Committee of the Whole regarding ongoing work on a leaf blower regulation ordinance.

items.title: Commendation of Building Commissioner Paul Moki
items.summary: Councilors congratulated Building Commissioner Paul Moki on his retirement after 38 years of service and passed a motion to invite him to a future meeting for a formal citation.

items.title: Snow and Ice Removal Ordinance
items.summary: The Council reconsidered and approved the snow and ice removal ordinance on its third reading.

items.title: DPW Sidewalk Repair Equipment
items.summary: Approved a request for the administration to price out sidewalk and stump grinding equipment for the DPW to assist in addressing a backlog of repairs.

items.title: Gig Economy Worker Classification Opposition
items.summary: The Council approved a resolution opposing state legislation and ballot initiatives that would classify gig economy workers as independent contractors rather than employees. Councilors argued the proposed changes would strip workers of essential benefits and increase the financial burden on municipal and state resources.

items.title: Eversource Project Updates
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that representatives from Eversource and the City Engineer attend a future meeting to provide updates on ongoing construction projects on Mystic Avenue and Winthrop Street.

items.title: Municipal Flag-Raising Policy Review
items.summary: The Council requested a report on current flag-raising practices and a plan to ensure city policies comply with the First Amendment following the Supreme Court decision in Shurtleff v. City of Boston.

items.title: MBTA Bus Network Redesign Feedback
items.summary: The Council referred the MBTA's bus network redesign proposal to the Committee of the Whole to host a public feedback session and invite transportation officials to discuss route changes.

items.title: Street Marking Restoration and Project Status
items.summary: Approved a request for Eversource to repaint crosswalks and bike lanes affected by construction and invited the Transportation Director to discuss the status of the work.

items.title: Routine Business and Adjournment
items.summary: The Council heard public participation, placed a National Grid grant of location paper on file, and adjourned the meeting.
